prompt: Very rarely, two customers get the same seat. It only happens during big on-sales when many people click at the same moment.
tells: many people click at the same moment
why: Two requests read "seat free" before either writes. Use a unique constraint or atomic compare-and-set.
trap: A cache could serve stale availability, but the double write itself needs atomicity to prevent.

prompt: An integration test passes alone every time but fails about one run in twenty when the suite runs in parallel.
tells: one run in twenty when the suite runs in parallel
why: Shared state between concurrent tests (a table, a file, a port) is racing.
trap: Retrying the flaky test hides the bug instead of finding the shared state.

prompt: A counter in a cache occasionally loses increments. When you add detailed logging around the update, the problem stops reproducing.
why: Logging changes timing and hides the race: a read-modify-write without atomicity. Use an atomic increment.
trap: Lost updates look like stale cache data, but they come from concurrent writes.

prompt: A cron job meant to run on one node occasionally runs on two at once after a node restarts.
tells: occasionally runs on two at once
why: Two nodes both think they hold the lock during handover. Use leases with fencing tokens.
trap: Skewed clocks can widen the window, but the bug is the unsafe handover.

prompt: Signup checks that an email isn't taken, then inserts the user. Rarely, two accounts end up with the same email.
tells: checks that an email isn't taken, then inserts
why: Two signups can both pass the check before either inserts; use a unique constraint.
trap: Check-then-act without a lock or constraint is a classic race.

prompt: Two admins edit the same product at the same time, and one admin's changes silently disappear.
tells: edit the same product at the same time
why: Last write wins; use version numbers (optimistic locking) to detect the conflict.
trap: Nothing blocked or errored, which is why it's a race and not contention.

prompt: A service crashes on startup about 1 time in 30 with a null config, depending on which of two background loaders finishes first.
tells: depending on which of two background loaders finishes first
why: Startup assumes an order that isn't guaranteed.
trap: Rare and timing-dependent are the two race signatures.

prompt: Users who double-click "Pay" are sometimes charged twice.
why: Two requests run concurrently; an idempotency key makes the second a no-op.
trap: Disabling the button helps, but the server must handle it too.
